Part: A. Approval hierarchy and people
Question: List every region and the districts under it. Does every district roll up to exactly one region?
Why it matters: Becomes the Entity hierarchy that the approval path follows.

Part: A. Approval hierarchy and people
Question: Are there entities that skip a level (e.g. province-level departments with no region, or a district reporting straight to the Mayor)?
Why it matters: Needs its own promotional path or an exception in the hierarchy.

Part: A. Approval hierarchy and people
Question: Is the budget entered only at district level, or also below it (departments, cost centres, wards inside a district)?
Why it matters: Decides whether the approval unit is the district or a lower member.

Part: A. Approval hierarchy and people
Question: Is there a level between Region and Mayor (budget office, finance department, treasury) that consolidates or adjusts numbers?
Why it matters: Adds a reviewer step, often with edit rights.

Part: A. Approval hierarchy and people
Question: Does the same approval path apply to Budget and Forecast, and to every version?
Why it matters: One hierarchy is tied to one Scenario + Version; different paths mean separate hierarchies.

Part: A. Approval hierarchy and people
Question: Will new districts be added during the year? Should they join the approval process automatically?
Why it matters: Drives the Auto Include setting.

Part: A. Approval hierarchy and people
Question: Who enters the budget in each district? How many people per district?
Why it matters: These are the district owners/preparers.

Part: A. Approval hierarchy and people
Question: If several people enter in one district, do they enter different parts (Opex vs Salaries vs Capex) or the same forms?
Why it matters: Different parts point to approval groups or a secondary dimension (Part C).

Part: A. Approval hierarchy and people
Question: Who approves at district level? Is it always a different person from the preparer?
Why it matters: Segregation of duties; first reviewer in the path.

Part: A. Approval hierarchy and people
Question: Who reviews at regional level? One person per region, or one person covering several regions?
Why it matters: Regional reviewer on the region parent member.

Part: A. Approval hierarchy and people
Question: Does the regional reviewer only review, or also change numbers before sending upward?
Why it matters: If they edit, they need Write security on those districts (Part D).

Part: A. Approval hierarchy and people
Question: Does the Mayor approve the whole province at once, or region by region?
Why it matters: Approving a parent approves all its children.

Part: A. Approval hierarchy and people
Question: Does anyone need to "sign off" (agree numbers but not yet approve), e.g. the Mayor's office before the Mayor?
Why it matters: Uses Sign Off status instead of a full approval step.

Part: A. Approval hierarchy and people
Question: When a reviewer rejects, should the budget go back one level or all the way to the district preparer?
Why it matters: Defines reject behaviour and who owns the unit after a reject.

Part: A. Approval hierarchy and people
Question: Do districts build bottom-up, or does the province first send targets or envelopes down to them?
Why it matters: Bottom Up vs Distribute template.

Part: A. Approval hierarchy and people
Question: Does the path ever change during the cycle (e.g. owner chooses who to send to next)?
Why it matters: Free Form template, where the user picks the next owner.

Part: B. Continuity: one person per level, or a group?
Question: For each level (district, region, Mayor), is one named person acceptable, or must someone else be able to act?
Why it matters: Decides user vs group as owner/reviewer.

Part: B. Continuity: one person per level, or a group?
Question: Name a backup for every level. Is the backup equal in authority, or only for leave and absence?
Why it matters: A backup with equal authority goes in the same group; leave-only cover can use delegation.

Part: B. Continuity: one person per level, or a group?
Question: Where a level has more than one reviewer, must all of them approve, or is any one enough?
Why it matters: All, in sequence = individual users. Any one = a group.

Part: B. Continuity: one person per level, or a group?
Question: If a group is the owner, should one person claim ownership first, or can anyone in the group act?
Why it matters: With a group owner and no one claiming, anyone in the group can act for it.

Part: B. Continuity: one person per level, or a group?
Question: Can a higher-level reviewer (e.g. region) take over a district's budget if the district is late?
Why it matters: Uses the Take Ownership action.

Part: B. Continuity: one person per level, or a group?
Question: Can an approver hand the unit to someone outside the normal path for a while (e.g. an expert)?
Why it matters: Uses the Delegate action.

Part: B. Continuity: one person per level, or a group?
Question: Who is the emergency override if a unit is stuck (owner left the organisation, wrong owner)?
Why it matters: Usually a Service Administrator changes status; name them.

Part: B. Continuity: one person per level, or a group?
Question: How many days can a unit sit with one person before it escalates? Escalate to whom?
Why it matters: Due dates and escalation in notifications or Task Manager.

Part: B. Continuity: one person per level, or a group?
Question: Must the audit trail show which individual acted when a group owns the unit?
Why it matters: Confirms group use is acceptable to internal audit.

Part: B. Continuity: one person per level, or a group?
Question: Is the Mayor's final approval allowed to be done by anyone else (deputy, chief of staff)?
Why it matters: The top level is the one most often left as a single person by policy.

Part: C. Approval groups: reviewing one slice of the budget
Question: Which parts of the budget need a different reviewer? (e.g. Opex, Revenue, Salaries/Workforce, Capex, Grants)
Why it matters: Each part is a candidate approval group.

Part: C. Approval groups: reviewing one slice of the budget
Question: For each part, who reviews it at district, region and province level?
Why it matters: Owner and reviewer per phase.

Part: C. Approval groups: reviewing one slice of the budget
Question: Must one part be approved and locked while another is still open?
Why it matters: Yes = phases (approval groups). No = one approval per district is enough.

Part: C. Approval groups: reviewing one slice of the budget
Question: Do the parts have to follow an order (e.g. Salaries before Opex), or run in parallel?
Why it matters: Sets the sequence of phases.

Part: C. Approval groups: reviewing one slice of the budget
Question: Is each part defined only by Account, or also by Department, Fund, Program or Project?
Why it matters: Defines the member selection of each approval group.

Part: C. Approval groups: reviewing one slice of the budget
Question: Does any account belong to two parts (e.g. salary-related Opex)? Which reviewer wins?
Why it matters: Overlapping cells need a clear rule; avoid overlap where possible.

Part: C. Approval groups: reviewing one slice of the budget
Question: Does the split differ by scenario (Budget = all accounts, Forecast = P&L only) or by period (quarter-end only)?
Why it matters: Approval groups can vary by scenario and period.

Part: C. Approval groups: reviewing one slice of the budget
Question: Does the Opex reviewer need to see Revenue and other parts (read only), or nothing outside Opex?
Why it matters: Decides whether Account security is needed (Part D).

Part: C. Approval groups: reviewing one slice of the budget
Question: Does the Mayor approve each part separately, or the complete district/province once all parts are done?
Why it matters: Final step per phase vs one final approval.

Part: C. Approval groups: reviewing one slice of the budget
Question: Are Capex and Workforce budgets prepared in their own modules with their own approvers?
Why it matters: Those may already need their own path or hierarchy.

Part: D. Security: how it all connects
Question: Where do users and groups come from: created in EPM, or synced from the client's identity system? Who owns group membership?
Why it matters: Group-based approvals depend on groups being kept up to date.

Part: D. Security: how it all connects
Question: Agree a group naming convention for preparers, approvers, reviewers and phase reviewers.
Why it matters: One group can then serve both security and approvals.

Part: D. Security: how it all connects
Question: For each role, fill in: entity access, account access, scenario/version access (Read / Write / None).
Why it matters: Becomes the access grant matrix.

Part: D. Security: how it all connects
Question: When the unit is with a reviewer, can they change numbers, or only comment and approve/reject?
Why it matters: Change = Write security; comment only = Read is enough.

Part: D. Security: how it all connects
Question: After a district promotes, should the preparer still see their budget (Read)?
Why it matters: After promotion the previous owner keeps Read only if security gives it.

Part: D. Security: how it all connects
Question: Can a district see other districts? Can a region see other regions?
Why it matters: Scope of Read access on Entity.

Part: D. Security: how it all connects
Question: Must the Opex reviewer be blocked from seeing other accounts, or is it enough that forms only show Opex?
Why it matters: Blocking needs Account security; hiding needs only form design. Account security adds admin and performance cost.

Part: D. Security: how it all connects
Question: Is Actual read-only for everyone? Who can write to the Final or Approved version?
Why it matters: Scenario and version security protect data outside approvals.

Part: D. Security: how it all connects
Question: Which business rules can each role run, and on which units?
Why it matters: Rules need launch access and run only on cells the user can write.

Part: D. Security: how it all connects
Question: Will users work in Smart View as well as web forms?
Why it matters: The same security applies; confirm users expect it.

Part: D. Security: how it all connects
Question: Who maintains owners, reviewers and security when staff change? How often?
Why it matters: Ongoing admin effort and the risk of stale owners.

Part: D. Security: how it all connects
Question: Does audit need a regular report of who has access to what?
Why it matters: Access-control and audit reports to plan for.

Part: E. Process controls, timing and locking
Question: Are there checks a district must pass before it can promote (e.g. no negative values, total within envelope)?
Why it matters: Data validation rules on forms.

Part: E. Process controls, timing and locking
Question: Should some conditions send the budget to an extra reviewer (e.g. new hires > 4 → HR review)?
Why it matters: Validation rules can change the promotional path.

Part: E. Process controls, timing and locking
Question: Is a comment required when rejecting, or when promoting with a variance above a threshold?
Why it matters: Annotations, form instructions, or a validation rule.

Part: E. Process controls, timing and locking
Question: What are the deadlines at each level (district submit, region review, Mayor approve)?
Why it matters: Due dates, Task Manager tasks, reminders.

Part: E. Process controls, timing and locking
Question: Who receives email at each step (owner, next reviewer, budget office)?
Why it matters: Notifiees and user email settings.

Part: E. Process controls, timing and locking
Question: After the Mayor approves, what must happen: lock only, copy Working to Final version, push to reporting?
Why it matters: Lock strategy and post-approval jobs.

Part: E. Process controls, timing and locking
Question: Who can reopen an approved budget, and under what conditions?
Why it matters: Reopen rights and change-control policy.

Part: E. Process controls, timing and locking
Question: How many budget rounds are expected (first draft, revised, final)? Should each round be kept?
Why it matters: Versions per round or one version with reopen.

Part: E. Process controls, timing and locking
Question: What status view does the budget office need (by district, by region, by phase)?
Why it matters: Approvals dashboard or a custom status report.

Part: E. Process controls, timing and locking
Question: Is there a hard cut-off after which no district can edit, whatever its status?
Why it matters: Freeze, scenario start/end periods, or version security.
